module_title: Anatomy of a Deed and Drafting Petitions
introduction: This intermediate tier explores the rigid, historical structure of a Conveyancing Deed, dissecting its non-operative and operative parts. It also covers the modern drafting mechanics for Bail Applications and Constitutional Writ Petitions.

core_concepts.title: The Structural Anatomy of a Deed
core_concepts.description:
Every formal conveyancing deed is drafted in a standard sequence:
1. Non-Operative Part:
   - Description/Title (e.g., 'THIS DEED OF SALE')
   - Date and Place
   - Parties (Names, ages, addresses of Vendor and Vendee)
   - Recitals (Starts with 'WHEREAS...'. Explains the history of the property and why the deed is being executed).
2. Operative Part:
   - Testatum ('NOW THIS DEED WITNESSETH AS FOLLOWS...'. The actual execution).
   - Habendum (Describes the estate being taken, usually starting with 'To have and to hold').
   - Exceptions and Reservations (Any rights held back by the seller).
   - Covenants (Promises, e.g., 'Seller promises the property is free from mortgages').
3. Formal Part: Testimonium, Signatures, and Attestation by witnesses.

core_concepts.title: Drafting a Bail Application (BNSS 2023 Context)
core_concepts.description:
Drafting bail requires hitting specific statutory and jurisprudential markers.
- Regular Bail (Section 480/483 BNSS): Drafted when the accused is already in police/judicial custody. Must state: No flight risk, willing to submit a surety bond, no risk of tampering with witnesses, and deep roots in society.
- Anticipatory Bail (Section 482 BNSS): Drafted when there is a 'reason to believe' an arrest is imminent for a non-bailable offense. Must highlight that the accusation is mala fide (made to humiliate), and the applicant will cooperate fully with the police investigation.

core_concepts.title: Drafting a Writ Petition (Article 226 / 32)
core_concepts.description:
A highly technical constitutional draft.
- Synopsis & List of Dates: Mandatory front-pages summarizing the timeline.
- Authority: Must clearly identify the 'State' or 'Authority' under Article 12 being sued.
- Grounds: Must explicitly state which Fundamental Right or legal right has been violated.
- Prayer: Must specifically ask for a particular writ (e.g., *Mandamus* to command an officer, *Certiorari* to quash an illegal government order).

core_concepts.title: Notice under Section 80 CPC
core_concepts.description: A mandatory drafting prerequisite. You cannot directly sue the Government. You MUST draft and serve a formal notice to the Government giving them **60 days** to resolve the issue before you can file a civil plaint. (Exception: You can bypass this with court permission only if seeking urgent/immediate relief).

important_entities.name: Habendum Clause
important_entities.key_fact: The 'To have and to hold' clause.
important_entities.significance: A highly tested definition in property law. The Habendum clause in a deed defines the extent of ownership or interest that is being granted (e.g., whether the property is given for life, for 99 years, or absolutely forever).

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Is an Affidavit a pleading under Order VI of the CPC? **NO**. An affidavit is sworn evidence, while pleadings are merely allegations. However, under the amended CPC (commercial suits) and BNSS, pleadings must often be *accompanied* by an affidavit to ensure parties do not make frivolous claims.

mnemonics_and_tricks.memory_phrase: T D P R T H (Title, Date, Parties, Recitals, Testatum, Habendum)
mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Use this sequence to structure any Deed (Sale, Lease, Mortgage) flawlessly in a drafting exam.

exam_strategy_tips: If asked to draft an Anticipatory Bail application, explicitly cite **Section 482 of the BNSS, 2023** (not the old Sec 438 CrPC), and emphasize that the 'applicant apprehends arrest due to political/personal enmity'.
